title: Migration 62 — status_history append-only and attributed
description: Applies a pre-62 world reproducing production's three status_history policies and its arwd grant exactly -- including the RESTRICTIVE overlay migration 22 creates -- then 62, runs 62's VERIFY A-G, then rolls 62 back on a disposable PostgreSQL cluster. status_history was the only log table with zero protective triggers and no actor column: compliance_audit_log and commercial_audit_log both carry two triggers each. The exposure is NOT the alarming-looking authenticated=arwd grant -- the operational-farmer policy is RESTRICTIVE, so it narrows access and never grants it, and the only PERMISSIVE policy admitting UPDATE or DELETE is the admin one. The real gap is that a DDP ADMINISTRATOR could rewrite or delete any row with nothing recording it, and that service_role and the table owner bypass RLS entirely and could additionally TRUNCATE. No policy can reach those roles; a trigger can. So 62 puts the guarantee in triggers, adds a changed_by forced from auth.uid(), and revokes UPDATE/DELETE from authenticated as a second layer rather than as the fix. Section G exists because the plausible wrong fix -- widening or dropping the RESTRICTIVE policy to make the grant look consistent -- would REMOVE a restriction while reading as hardening.

verify.note: B, C and D are the point, and they run as a SUPERUSER on purpose: the superuser is one of the roles the pre-62 table could not restrain, so proving refusal for an under-privileged role would prove nothing. D is separate from B and C because a row-level trigger never fires for TRUNCATE -- a table guarded only by the row-level trigger is still emptiable in one statement -- and it carries a catalog interlock so it never attempts the statement unless the guard is already proven present. F asserts the ABSENCE of a column DEFAULT on changed_by: a default would satisfy 'attribution exists' while remaining overridable by any caller, which is the forgery the BEFORE INSERT trigger prevents. G asserts the migration did NOT touch the policies, and is the section that catches the tempting wrong fix.
